blocks.text: Ad-Dayyaan is a confirmed Name of Allaah in the sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ.

"I purchased a camel and rode it hard for a month until I reached Syria. 'Abdullah ibn Unays was there, and I sent word to him, saying, 'Jabir is at the door.' The messenger returned and said, 'Jabir ibn 'Abdullah?' 'Yes,' I replied. So 'Abdullah came out and embraced me. I said, 'A hadith reached me which I had not heard before and I feared that one of us might die.'" He went on, "I heard the Prophet ﷺ say, 'Allah will gather His slaves or people naked, uncircumcised, without anything.' We asked, 'What is meant by "without anything"?' The Prophet ﷺ said, 'They will have nothing with them.' 'They will be called by a voice that is heard from afar (and I think that he said, 'as if it was from close at hand'), saying, "I am the King, I am the Supreme Judge. None of the people of the Fire will enter the Fire while any of the people of the Garden are seeking him for an injustice he did to him. None of the people of the Garden will enter the Garden while any of the people of the Fire are seeking him for some injustice he did to him. Even for a slap."' I asked, 'How is this? We come to Allah naked and without any worldly goods?' He said, 'This applies to good actions and evil actions.'"
blocks.ref: Ahmad, Al-Musnad 3/495; Bukhaaree, Al-Adab al-Mufrad 970; Ibn Abee 'Aasim, As-Sunnah 514; Al-Haakim, Al-Mustadrak 2/437; and others

blocks.text: Al-Haakim added, "The Messenger of Allaah ﷺ recited,
This Day shall every person be recompensed for what he earned. No injustice (shall be done to anybody).

Ad-Dayyaan The Supreme Judge means the One who rewards or punishes, the One to take Account. Allaah will gather together the first and the last people on the Day of Resurrection naked without clothes, barefooted without footwear, uncircumcised and standing without any worldly possessions. Then He will reward or punish them and bring them to account for what they have put forward in their worldly life of deeds – if they were good then it will be good and if they were bad then it will be bad.

If an intelligent person knows that the Lord is The Supreme Judge and that the Day of Resurrection is a day of recompense and account, and that he will meet Allaah on that Day without any doubt, and that on that Day he will find all of his deeds that he performed brought forth – the good deeds and the bad, the fine deeds and the evil ones. Indeed he will prepare to be taken to account for that day and ready his provisions.

The astute clever person is the one who passes judgement upon himself and takes himself to account whilst he has respite in this life to do so and has time to do good deeds. The weak person is the one who is heedless of it which comes from being in sin and error and following his desires until regret suddenly comes upon him. A poet spoke about this with the following words:

And by Allaah indeed oppression is despicable.
The evil doer is still in his plentiful oppression.
To the Judge on the Day of Judgement we pass away,
And in front of Allah those who have grievances will gather.
The rightly guided Khaleefah 'Umar bin Al-Khattaab said,

"Bring yourselves to account before you are brought to account. Weigh your deeds before they are weighed. It will be easier for your account tomorrow if you bring yourselves to account today. Beautify yourselves for the greatest exhibition – on that Day you will be brought for judgement and nothing will be hidden from amongst you."
blocks.ref: Ibn Abee ad-Dunyaa, Muhaasibatun Nafs no. 2

keyPoints: Ad-Dayyaan is a confirmed Name of Allaah in the sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ, in the hadeeth of Jaabir from 'Abdullah ibn Unays: "I am the King, I am the Supreme Judge."
Ad-Dayyaan means the One who rewards or punishes, the One to take Account.
Allaah will gather the first and the last people on the Day of Resurrection naked, barefooted, uncircumcised and without any worldly possessions, then reward or punish them for their deeds.
Whoever knows that the Lord is The Supreme Judge and that the Day of Resurrection is a day of recompense and account will prepare for that Day and ready his provisions.
The astute person takes himself to account whilst he has respite in this life, while the weak person is heedless until regret suddenly comes upon him.

evidence.text: "I am the King, I am the Supreme Judge. None of the people of the Fire will enter the Fire while any of the people of the Garden are seeking him for an injustice he did to him..."
This Day shall every person be recompensed for what he earned. No injustice (shall be done to anybody).

recall.a: The Supreme Judge: the One who rewards or punishes, the One to take Account.

recall.q: Where is the Name Ad-Dayyaan confirmed?
recall.a: In the sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ, in the hadeeth Jaabir bin 'Abdullaah travelled a month to Syria to hear from 'Abdullah ibn Unays: "I am the King, I am the Supreme Judge."

recall.q: Which aayah did the Messenger of Allaah ﷺ recite, according to Al-Haakim's addition?
recall.a: "This Day shall every person be recompensed for what he earned. No injustice (shall be done to anybody)." [Ghaafir 40:17]

recall.q: Who is the astute clever person according to the chapter?
recall.a: The one who passes judgement upon himself and takes himself to account whilst he has respite in this life and has time to do good deeds.

recall.q: What did 'Umar bin Al-Khattaab say about taking oneself to account?
recall.a: "Bring yourselves to account before you are brought to account. Weigh your deeds before they are weighed..."
